phase_0.boundary_condition: The whole-chain atomic conformation operator that contains the local contact-map composition and enforces global mechanical stability via fixed-point closure.

⊢.justification: The void state before any specific donor-acceptor contact is established or chirality is resolved; the chain exists as a linear sequence without defined tertiary structure.

⊣.justification: The terminal anchor that defines the closed boundary of the system; it contains all local interactions and enforces the global constraint of mechanical stability.

≻.justification: The forward morphism where local donor-acceptor pairs are composed into the whole-chain structure, propagating constraints from local to global.

≺.justification: The reverse transformation where global stability requirements descend to constrain local contact geometries, ensuring the local pairs satisfy the global fixed-point condition.

⋈.justification: The sequential chaining of local contact pairs into a coherent global map; each contact is composed with the next to build the full structural network.

⊙.justification: The self-reference of the persistent chirality; the structural handedness is an intrinsic property that remains invariant under the folding process.

∈.justification: The split into two arms: one arm selects a valid donor-acceptor pair from the bank, the other arm evaluates the alternative pairs that are rejected or held in reserve.

∋.justification: The rejoining of the selected contact and the rejected alternatives into a single resolved state; the selected contact is committed, and the rejected ones are banked as alternatives.

⊤.justification: The affirmative state where a donor-acceptor pair satisfies the geometric and matrix relations required for a stable contact.

⊥.justification: The negative state where a donor-acceptor pair fails to satisfy the geometric or matrix relations, leading to rejection.

⊞.justification: The state where both left-handed and right-handed chirality are held simultaneously in the local frame, a contradiction that is kept live without resolution until the global constraint forces a choice.

⊡.justification: The irreversible fixation of the final conformation; once the fixed-point is reached, the structure is mechanically stable and cannot be undone without breaking the chain.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the unfolded polypeptide chain as the void state
Establish the whole-chain folding operator as the terminal anchor
Begin forward composition of local contact pairs into the global map
Split the bank of candidate donor-acceptor pairs into selected and rejected arms
Evaluate the selected arm for valid geometric and matrix relations
Evaluate the rejected arm for invalid relations
Hold the chirality conflict in the local frame if both handedness are present
Rejoin the selected and rejected arms into a resolved contact state
Compose the resolved contact with the next contact in the chain
Propagate global stability constraints back to the local contact frame
Assert the chirality identity of the resolved contact
Continue forward composition with the next contact pair
Split the next bank of candidate pairs
Evaluate the next selected arm
Evaluate the next rejected arm
Rejoin the next resolved contact state
Compose the next resolved contact
Propagate constraints again
Assert chirality identity again
Fix the final conformation at the fixed-point closure
Confirm the whole-chain operator has reached mechanical stability

phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The sequential composition order that processes contact pairs in the order they appear in the chain, with backtracking allowed for constraint resolution
phase_5.alfs_store: The initial unfolded chain and the set of geometric and matrix relations that define valid contacts

phase_6.cycle_cost: The computational effort to evaluate geometric and matrix relations for each candidate contact pair
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Unfolded chain with a bank of candidate contacts and no resolved structure
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Folded chain with a resolved contact map and fixed-point closure
